claim.quote: The detector, consisting of eight NaI(Tl) crystals with a total mass of 99.1 kg, has been relocated to Yemilab, a new underground facility in Korea, and features direct PMT-coupling technology to enhance sensitivity.

name: Upgrading the COSINE-100 Experiment for Enhanced Sensitivity to Low-Mass Dark Matter Detection

summary.plain: The COSINE-100 detector was upgraded and moved to Yemilab as COSINE-100U, with its photomultipliers coupled directly to the eight crystals (99.1 kg in all) to collect more light and probe lighter dark matter.
summary.technical: Design and upgrade paper: relocation to Yemilab, improved light collection and reduced background; the abstract recalls that COSINE-100 found no significant annual-modulation signal, with a discrepancy of more than 3 sigma with DAMA/LIBRA (Commun. Phys. 8, 135 (2025)).

title: Upgrading the COSINE-100 Experiment for Enhanced Sensitivity to Low-Mass Dark Matter Detection
why_it_matters: Documents the upgraded detector that continues the DAMA/LIBRA test at a deeper site.
